author: Rahul kp
title: Recoverable Amount
simple_words: If the asset's book value is more than what you can recover from it, write down the extra as impairment loss.

definitions.meaning: Higher of an asset's fair value less costs of disposal and its value in use.
Present value of future cash flows expected from continuing use of the asset and its final disposal.

key_points: Impairment loss arises when ==carrying amount== is more than recoverable amount.
Recoverable amount = higher of ==FVLCD== and ==value in use==.
If either one is above carrying amount, there is no impairment and the other need not be estimated.
Loss goes to profit or loss, unless the asset is carried at revalued amount (treated as revaluation decrease first).

formulas.name: Fair value less costs of disposal
formulas.legend: FV = fair value (price in an orderly transaction); CD = incremental costs of disposal

formulas.name: Recoverable amount
formulas.legend: RA = recoverable amount; VIU = value in use (PV of future cash flows)

formulas.name: Impairment loss
formulas.legend: CA = carrying amount; RA = recoverable amount. If CA ≤ RA, loss is nil.

insight.text: Ind AS 36 takes the higher of the two values, so the asset is written down by the smaller amount.

memory_trick.mnemonic: Sell or Use? Take the Higher
memory_trick.explanation: Management could sell the asset (FVLCD) or keep using it (VIU). A sensible owner picks the better route, so RA is the higher value.

exam_tip: Write the formula first, then state which of FVLCD or VIU is higher. Marks are given for the choice and the reason.

doubt.question: Must I always compute both FVLCD and VIU?
doubt.answer: No. If one of them is already above carrying amount, the asset is not impaired and the other need not be estimated.

mistakes.wrong: Taking the lower of FVLCD and VIU as recoverable amount
mistakes.right: Recoverable amount is the !!higher!! of FVLCD and value in use.

mistakes.wrong: Using fair value without deducting costs of disposal
mistakes.right: Deduct incremental costs of disposal from fair value to get FVLCD.

mistakes.wrong: Including finance costs and income tax cash flows in value in use
mistakes.right: VIU cash flows exclude financing activities and income tax receipts or payments.

mistakes.wrong: Discounting VIU cash flows at a post-tax rate
mistakes.right: Use a !!pre-tax!! discount rate that reflects current market assessments of time value and asset-specific risks.

applicability: Ind AS 36 Impairment of Assets (as notified, applicable)
